simple.meaning: שַׁפִּיר (shappîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “beautiful.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שַׁפִּיר (H8209) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 4:9, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁפִּיר (H8209) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שַׁפִּיר (H8209) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שַׁפִּיר (shappîyr) / H8209 is traced through Daniel 4:9, Daniel 4:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.

timeline.evidenceText: “Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.

“This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
